name: log-what-broke
query: Note that the install for that vector DB fails on Python 3.13 - we hit it twice today.
why: The RECORD job. First-hand experience with a catalogued tool, with the version condition that makes the note falsifiable rather than an opinion.

name: log-what-worked
query: The parser we picked chewed through a two hundred thousand page run without a hitch. Write that down so we don't re-litigate it next quarter.
why: A works verdict is as much a field note as a broken one, and notes are append-only so both stay in the record.

name: discover-new-tools
query: Any new agent frameworks worth adding? Give the tooling catalog a refresh pass.
why: The DISCOVER job: scan the seed sources, confirm each candidate, then dedupe-ingest through ledger.py rather than pasting links in by hand.

name: fold-in-a-pile-of-links
query: Here are eight repos I collected this week. Fold them into the AI tooling catalog.
why: Ingest with the duplicate guard. Already-known URLs report unchanged, and github repos with no seed-sections entry land in triage for classification.

name: check-for-staleness
query: Check the AI catalog for staleness - which entries haven't been verified in the last three months?
why: The VERIFY job on both axes: liveness probing that URLs still resolve, and the more valuable claims queue on map rows whose assertions are unverified.

name: correct-a-wrong-entry
query: The map still lists that RAG framework as active but I'm fairly sure it was archived. Can you check and fix the entry?
why: Verification aimed at correcting the record, which is the discriminator against ai-engineering: the deliverable is an updated dated row, not an answer.

name: documented-flag-does-not-exist
query: That flag the docs told us to pass doesn't exist in the current release. Second time this week their docs have been wrong.
why: The hardest positive: no maintenance pass was asked for and there is no explicit request at all, but a tool in the corpus was used and something was learned, which is exactly when a note gets recorded.

name: options-question
query: What are my options for a vector store if we're OSS-only?
why: Belongs to ai-engineering, the read path. Nothing about the corpus is changing; the user wants an answer out of it.

name: is-it-maintained-for-a-decision
query: Is LangGraph still maintained? I'm deciding whether to start a new build on it.
why: Belongs to ai-engineering. Deliberate contrast with the correct-a-wrong-entry case: the user wants the answer, not a corrected row, so this reads the corpus rather than writing it.

name: bootstrap-a-repo
query: Bootstrap a RAG repo over our internal docs.
why: Belongs to ai-agent-project-scaffold. Corpus changes may come out of that run later, but the request is to stand up a project.

name: bare-research-request
query: Research whether the small open-weight models handle function calling well. I want sources and dates.
why: Belongs to deep-research. This skill wraps deep-research during a maintenance pass, but a research question with no corpus intent goes straight there, and folding the result in is offered afterward.

name: update-a-project-readme
query: Update our README to describe the new agent module we added.
why: Ordinary documentation work in the user's own project, which goes to agent-skills. This skill's write path only ever touches the shared tooling corpus under resources/, so guards against firing on the verb update near the word agent.

name: refresh-a-data-catalog
query: Our data catalog has stale table descriptions. Can we refresh them?
why: A warehouse metadata chore that belongs to data-engineering. Shares the words catalog, stale and refresh with this skill and shares nothing else.
